newsitem.title: KENYA: Meeting to negotiate deal on toxic chemicals.
newsitem.headline: Meeting to negotiate deal on toxic chemicals.

text.p: Officials from 100 governments will meet in Nairobi on Monday to negotiate an international agreement on hazardous chemicals and pesticides, the Nairobi-based United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) said.
UNEP officials on Sunday said the talks would lead to a legally-binding treaty to regulate the import and export of hazardous chemicals.
Maria Celina de Azevedo Rodriques, a Brazilian diplomat who will chair the meeting, said: "Once in place, this new treaty will represent our first line of defence against chemical hazards."
A Prior Informed Consent (PIC) procedure already exists on a voluntary basis to enable countries to learn about the characteristics of hazardous chemicals that may be shipped into the country.
Once the proposed treaty comes into force, the procedures will be strengthened so that governments can decide whether or not to permit imports of specified chemicals.

The first negotiating session on a PIC treaty was held in Brussels last March. After the Nairobi meeting another negotiating session, probably in Rotterdam early in 1997, is expected to adopt the final treaty.
